teleport.kid: Instantly zooms you (or anyone) to another spot or to another player.
ex: Jump 20 blocks straight up into the sky.
Go to the exact spot x=0, y=100, z=0.
Bring every player to where you are.
teleport.tip: /tp is the short name for /teleport. They do the same thing.
teleport.block: In a command block, ~ ~ ~ means the block's spot, not yours. Use /tp @p 100 64 200 to send the nearest player to a fixed place, like a teleporter pad.

spawnpoint.kid: Sets where a player comes back to life after they die.
spawnpoint.block: Put it on a button at the start of a parkour level so players restart at that checkpoint: /spawnpoint @p ~ ~1 ~

clearspawnpoint.kid: Erases a player's personal respawn spot, so they go back to the world spawn.

setworldspawn.kid: Moves the world's main starting spot, where new players appear.
ex: Make where you're standing the new world spawn.

spreadplayers.kid: Scatters players (or mobs) to random safe spots around a center point. Great for starting a survival game.
ex: Scatter everyone up to 100 blocks away, at least 10 blocks apart.
Scatter everyone up to 100 blocks away, at least 10 blocks apart.
spreadplayers.tip: The two numbers are: how far apart they must be, then how far away they can go.

locate.kid: Tells you the coordinates of the nearest village, temple, biome, and more.
ex: Find the closest village of any kind.
locate.tip: It tells you where, it doesn't take you there. Use /tp with the numbers it gives you. On Java you can click the green coordinates in chat to teleport!

ride.kid: Makes one thing ride on top of another, like you riding a pig or a chicken riding a zombie.

rotate.kid: Turns a player or mob to face a direction or look at something.
ex: Turn around to face north, looking straight ahead.

spectate.kid: When you're in Spectator mode, lets you see through another player's or mob's eyes.
ex: Ride along inside the nearest bee's view.
spectate.tip: You have to be in Spectator mode first: /gamemode spectator

give.kid: Puts any item right into a player's inventory.
ex: Get a full stack of 64 diamonds.
Get a command block (you'll need it for the Command Blocks lessons!).
give.tip: Item names use underscores instead of spaces: golden_apple, oak_log, ender_pearl. Start typing and the game will suggest names.
give.block: Put /give @p diamond 1 on a button to make a prize button. @p means the player standing closest to the block.

clear.kid: Removes items from a player's inventory. With no item named, it empties EVERYTHING.

enchant.kid: Adds an enchantment to the item the player is holding.
ex: Make the sword in your hand super sharp.
Make your pickaxe dig super fast.
enchant.tip: Hold the item in your hand first! It only works on items that could get that enchantment normally.

item.kid: Puts an item into an exact slot, like a helmet slot or a chest slot, replacing what's there.
ex: Wear a pumpkin on your head.
Put a shield in your other hand.

replaceitem.kid: Puts an item into an exact slot, like a helmet slot or a chest slot, replacing what's there.
ex: Wear a pumpkin on your head.
Put a shield in your other hand.

loot.kid: Gives out a random set of items, the same way a treasure chest or a defeated mob would.
ex: Get the loot from a dungeon chest.
Get the loot from a dungeon chest.

recipe.kid: Unlocks (or locks) recipes in the recipe book.

xp.kid: Gives or takes away experience (the green XP bar you use for enchanting).
ex: Get 30 levels, enough for top enchantments.
Get 30 levels. The L means levels.
Get 100 XP points (no L means points).
xp.tip: On Java the full name is /experience; /xp is the shortcut.

setblock.kid: Places one block at an exact spot.
ex: Turn the block under your feet into diamond.
Put a torch 2 blocks east of you.
setblock.block: Command blocks + /setblock can build doors that open and close: one button runs /setblock x y z air, another puts the block back.

fill.kid: Fills a whole box-shaped area with one kind of block. Super fast building!
ex: Build a glass room around you (hollow = empty inside).
Make a flat 11×11 grass floor under you.
Clear out all the blocks around you.
fill.tip: You give two corners of the box. The first three numbers are one corner, the next three are the opposite corner. Endings: hollow (empty inside), outline (walls only, keeps the inside), keep (only fills empty air), destroy (breaks blocks so they drop).

clone.kid: Copies a box of blocks and pastes it somewhere else, like copy and paste for builds.
ex: Copy the 6×6×6 box next to you and paste it 10 blocks east.
clone.tip: First two spots are the corners of what to copy. The last spot is where the copy's lowest, north-west corner goes.

place.kid: Instantly places a whole natural thing, like a tree or a village, the way the world would make it.
ex: Grow an oak tree right here.
Build a plains village right here.

structure.kid: Saves a build so you can load copies of it anywhere, anytime.
ex: Save the 11×11×11 box next to you as "myhouse".
Paste a copy of "myhouse" right here.
structure.tip: On Java, use a Structure Block instead (/give @s structure_block).

fillbiome.kid: Changes the biome of an area, which changes grass color, music, and more.
ex: Turn the area around you into a cherry grove.
fillbiome.tip: You might need to leave and come back before the colors update.

testforblock.kid: Checks whether a certain block is at a spot. Used in command block contraptions.
ex: Is there a diamond block on top of this command block?
testforblock.tip: Newer way that works on both editions: /execute if block ... run ...

testforblocks.kid: Checks whether two areas have exactly the same blocks, like a build-matching puzzle.
ex: Does the area at 10 64 0 match the pattern at 0 64 0?

summon.kid: Makes a mob or thing appear out of nowhere.
ex: Make a pig appear on you.
summon.tip: Careful with dangerous mobs like the Wither! Try in a test world first.

kill.kid: Instantly removes players, mobs, or dropped items.
ex: Clean up every dropped item lying on the ground.
kill.tip: ⚠️ NEVER type /kill @e by itself. @e means every entity, so it removes ALL mobs, pets, item frames, armor stands... and you!

effect.kid: Gives potion powers (or takes them away), like speed, jump boost, or night vision.
ex: Run super fast for 60 seconds (power level 3).
See in the dark forever, with no swirly particles.
Run super fast for 60 seconds (power level 3).
See in the dark forever, with no swirly particles.
effect.tip: The numbers are: how many seconds, then strength. Strength starts at 0, so 0 = level I, 1 = level II, 2 = level III. The true at the end hides the particles.
effect.block: Speed pad! A Repeat command block, Always Active, with: /execute as @a at @s if block ~ ~-1 ~ gold_block run effect ... (see the Command Blocks lessons).

damage.kid: Hurts a player or mob by a certain amount. Each heart is 2 points.
ex: Hit the nearest zombie for 2 hearts.
Hit the nearest zombie for 2 hearts.

tag.kid: Sticks an invisible name-label on a player or mob so commands can find them later.
ex: Later, [tag=hero] picks only tagged players. This brings the heroes to you.
tag.tip: Tags are perfect for games: tag players on the red team, players who found the secret, etc.

attribute.kid: Changes a player's or mob's built-in stats, like size, speed, or max health.

event.kid: Triggers a special built-in change on a mob, like making a creeper charged.
ex: Turn the nearest creeper into a charged creeper.

playanimation.kid: Makes a mob or player play one of their animations once.

swing.kid: Makes a player or mob swing their arm, like they're hitting something.

data.kid: Reads or changes the hidden details (called NBT data) stored inside mobs, blocks, and items.
ex: See exactly how much health you have.
Freeze the nearest pig like a statue.

gamemode.kid: Switches between Survival, Creative, Adventure, and Spectator.
ex: Fly through walls as a ghost (Bedrock: newer versions).
Everyone can play but not break blocks. Perfect for maps you build.

defaultgamemode.kid: Sets which game mode new players start in.

difficulty.kid: Changes how hard the game is: peaceful, easy, normal, or hard.
ex: No hostile mobs, and you never get hungry.
Tougher mobs. Hunger can knock you down to half a heart.

time.kid: Changes the time of day, or pauses it.
ex: Stop the sun and moon from moving. /time resume starts it again.
time.tip: A whole Minecraft day is 24000 ticks (20 real minutes). You can also use numbers: /time set 6000 is noon.

daylock.kid: Freezes time so it never turns night (or unfreezes it).
ex: Lock the time. Do /time set day first for forever daytime.

weather.kid: Makes it sunny, rainy, or thunderstormy.

toggledownfall.kid: Switches rain on if it's off, or off if it's on.
ex: Flip the rain on or off.

gamerule.kid: Changes the world's rules, like keeping your stuff when you die or stopping fire from spreading.
ex: Keep all your items when you die.
Creepers can't blow up blocks, endermen can't take blocks.
Stop command blocks from spamming chat.
Keep all your items when you die.
Creepers can't blow up blocks, endermen can't take blocks.
Stop command blocks from spamming chat.
gamerule.tip: The rule names are spelled differently! Java uses underscores (keep_inventory). Bedrock squishes the words together (keepinventory). Type /gamerule and a space to see the full list.

worldborder.kid: Puts an invisible wall around the world so nobody can go too far.
ex: Center it on where you're standing.
Shrink it to 20 wide over 60 seconds. Battle royale!

tick.kid: Controls the speed of the whole game world: freeze it, slow it down, or speed it up.
ex: Freeze everything! Mobs, water, and redstone all stop. (You can still move.)

tickingarea.kid: Keeps a part of the world running even when no player is near it, so farms and command blocks keep working.
ex: Keep the area around you always running.

forceload.kid: Keeps a part of the world running even when no player is near it.
ex: Keep the chunk you're in always loaded.

mobevent.kid: Turns certain mob events, like pillager patrols or wandering traders, on or off.
ex: Stop pillager patrols from showing up.

seed.kid: Shows the world's seed, the secret number that made your world. Share it so friends can make the same world!
seed.tip: On Bedrock, the seed is shown in World Settings.

say.kid: Posts a message in chat for everyone, with your name in front.
say.block: From a command block, the message shows as [@] Hello. Nice for announcements.

tell.kid: Sends a secret message only one player can see.
ex: /tell Steve meet me at the castle

me.kid: Posts an action message, like * Alex is dancing.

title.kid: Shows BIG text in the middle of the screen, or small text above the hotbar.
ex: Giant text in the middle of everyone's screen.
Smaller text under the title. Do this one first, then the title.
Giant text in the middle of everyone's screen.
Smaller text under the title. Do this one first, then the title.
title.block: Put a pressure plate in your doorway with a command block underneath: /title @p title "Welcome!"

titleraw.kid: Like /title, but uses fancy JSON text so you can mix colors and show scores.

tellraw.kid: Sends a chat message with colors and no name in front. It uses a special format called JSON.
ex: A gold message in chat. §6 means gold.
tellraw.tip: Watch the punctuation carefully: every { needs a }, and every quote " needs a partner.

teammsg.kid: Sends a message only your team can see.

dialog.kid: Shows a pop-up window with text and buttons. These are made with data packs.

dialogue.kid: Opens the talking window of an NPC (a villager-like character you set up in Education/creator worlds).

bossbar.kid: Makes your own boss health bar at the top of the screen.
ex: Create a bar named Dragon Lord.

playsound.kid: Plays any sound from the game.
playsound.tip: Sound names are different on each edition. Start typing and let the suggestions help.

particle.kid: Makes sparkles, hearts, smoke, flames, and other visual effects appear.
ex: A burst of 10 hearts above you.
particle.block: A Repeat command block running /particle makes a never-ending fountain of sparkles.

music.kid: Plays or stops the background music.
ex: Fade out the music over 2 seconds.

camerashake.kid: Shakes the player's screen, like an earthquake!

camera.kid: Takes control of a player's camera: fade the screen, change zoom, or move the view like a movie.
ex: Fade to black for 1 second, stay 2, fade back in 1.
Give the camera back to normal.

fog.kid: Adds or removes fog settings that come from add-on packs.

posteffect.kid: Puts a screen filter on a player's view, like blur or upside-down colors.
ex: Flip all the colors on your screen.
See the world like a creeper (green and pixel-y).

hud.kid: Hides or shows parts of the screen, like the hotbar or hearts.
ex: Hide everything for a clean screenshot.

waypoint.kid: Changes how players show up on the locator bar (the bar that points toward other players).
ex: Make your dot red on everyone's locator bar.

execute.kid: The super-command! It runs another command, but only for certain players, at certain places, or when something is true. Read it like a sentence: as WHO, at WHERE, if SOMETHING, run THIS.
ex: For every player, at their spot, summon a chicken.
/execute as @a at @s if block ~ ~-1 ~ gold_block run effect give @s speed 2 2 true
Anyone standing on gold gets speed.
/execute as @a at @s if block ~ ~-1 ~ gold_block run effect @s speed 2 2 true
Anyone standing on gold gets speed.
/execute if entity @e[type=zombie,distance=..10] run say Zombie nearby!
Warn if a zombie is close.
/execute if entity @e[type=zombie,r=10] run say Zombie nearby!
Warn if a zombie is close.
execute.tip: There's a whole lesson on this in Command Blocks → Commands inside commands.
execute.block: Most cool command block tricks use /execute in a Repeat block set to Always Active.

scoreboard.kid: Keeps score! Make points, kill counts, timers, and show them on the side of the screen.
ex: Show it on the right side of the screen.
scoreboard.tip: dummy means "only commands change this score."
scoreboard.block: Put /scoreboard players add @p points 1 on a button for a point-scoring button.

testfor.kid: Checks if any player or mob matches what you're looking for. Used with comparators and Conditional command blocks.
ex: Is any player within 5 blocks of this command block?

function.kid: Runs a whole list of commands saved in a file (from a data pack on Java, or a behavior pack on Bedrock).

schedule.kid: Runs a function later, after a delay.
ex: Run the boom function in 5 seconds.

random.kid: Rolls a random number, like dice.
ex: Roll a six-sided die and show everyone.
Pick a secret random number from 1 to 100.

return.kid: Stops a function early and sends back a number.

trigger.kid: Lets regular players (not operators) change a special score, often by clicking chat buttons in custom maps.
ex: Add 1 to your vote score (only if a map maker enabled it).

compute.kid: Calculates a number, including random numbers, for data pack makers.
ex: Roll a random number from 1 to 6.

stopwatch.kid: Makes a timer that counts up. Great for timing races and parkour.

team.kid: Makes teams with colors. Teammates' names show in the team color.

advancement.kid: Gives or takes away advancements (the achievement pop-ups on Java).

scriptevent.kid: Sends a message to scripts in an add-on.

inputpermission.kid: Turns a player's controls on or off, like stopping them from moving or looking around.

controlscheme.kid: Changes how the player's controls work, for special camera setups made by creators.

aimassist.kid: Turns on aim assist, which gently helps a player aim at things.

help.kid: Lists commands and shows how to type them.

op.kid: Makes a player an operator, which means they can use commands.

deop.kid: Takes away a player's operator powers.

kick.kid: Removes a player from the game. They can join again.

ban.kid: Bans a player from a server so they can't come back.

ban-ip.kid: Bans a computer's internet address from a server.

whitelist.kid: Controls the list of players allowed to join a server.

allowlist.kid: Controls the list of players allowed to join a server.

permission.kid: Reloads who is allowed to do what on a dedicated server.

save.kid: Controls saving the world on a server (for making backups).

reload.kid: Reloads data packs (Java) or behavior pack functions and scripts (Bedrock) after you change them.

transfer.kid: Sends a player to a different server.

setidletimeout.kid: Kicks players who stay still too long on a server.

setmaxplayers.kid: Sets how many players can join.

publish.kid: Opens your single-player world to others on your home network (LAN).

unpublish.kid: Closes your world to LAN players.

changesetting.kid: Changes a setting on a dedicated server while it's running.

reloadconfig.kid: Reloads a dedicated server's settings files.

reloadpacketlimitconfig.kid: Reloads a dedicated server's network limit settings.

serveridentity.kid: Manages a dedicated server's identity key.

editor-allowlist.kid: Controls who can use Bedrock Editor mode on a server.

sendshowstoreoffer.kid: Shows a Marketplace store offer to a player (used by servers).

datapack.kid: Turns data packs on or off and lists them.
ex: See which data packs are installed.

version.kid: Tells you which version of the game is running.

fetchprofile.kid: Looks up a player's account name, ID, and skin.
ex: Show your own profile, with a button to get your own head!

debug.kid: Records how fast the game is running, for finding lag.

jfr.kid: Records detailed performance info for experts.

perf.kid: Records 10 seconds of performance info on a server.

test.kid: Runs automatic tests that game makers build to check their creations.

gametest.kid: Runs automatic tests that add-on makers build.

wsserver.kid: Connects the game to an outside coding tool (a WebSocket server).

project.kid: Manages a project in Bedrock Editor mode.

packstack.kid: Lists which resource and behavior packs are loaded.
